method: Re-established the required and restricted groups from the 2026–2027 UvA curriculum and re-read the project entry, methods courses, major comparison matches and UCR workbook evidence before judging the exact frozen canonical and decision.
findings: The dated catalogue has 60 required credits in year one. Year two has 48 required credits and 12 chosen from three named courses. Year three has 30 open credits, the required 6-EC Reflection on Digital Culture and 18-EC project, and one 6-EC selection. Logic and Society is illustrated. The catalogue requires the whole first and second years before the final project, with possible individual dispensation. Modern Databases supports the Data Management and Governance Project, and interactive-systems research methods and advanced programming support Systeemproject.

The workbook supplies a direct, sustained systems and data basis for a broad response, a separate mathematical and computational focus, and a human-centred focus supported by cognitive science, qualitative research and product design. The latter uses customer journeys and applied research, with limits relative to dedicated digital interaction design. The final distinctness totals are 37.5, 52.5 and 82.5 EC each way. No additional option is needed at the maximum.

The overlap between Reflection on Digital Culture and AI Ethics covers ethical frameworks, privacy and social responsibility. Deep learning directly supports the required Data Science unit’s Python modelling and evaluation, while data visualisation is directly represented by the introductory UCR data course. Organisational strategy has a stronger connection with Information and Knowledge Management than with specialist compliance architecture. Semantic Web, the dedicated projects and the compulsory thesis remain separate. Optional UCR research is comparison-only.

The normal renderer selects the three reviewed option concepts and programme overview. The 28 comparator titles, 36 unique UCR titles and descriptions, nine note references and source destinations agree with their reviewed inputs. The six terms for each programme account for 180 EC.
